lens4_audits.public_summary: Across 10 dated Graziano-group texts from 2011 to 2026, core Attention Schema Theory components (perceptual models, social attribution of awareness, and simplified shell models) appear in 2011 alongside Micah Blumberg’s 2011-2025 genealogy, followed by model-based attention control (2015), distributed self-models (2018), and information conservation (2022). Four neural-network self-modeling components (trained self-modeling networks, auxiliary internal-state prediction, weight/RLCT restructuring, and implemented self-modeling architectures) first appear together in June 2024 and persist in the 2026 Version of Record, after Micah’s 2011-2022 self-learning and self-predicting network notes. This private result is component-level and uncalibrated, with 12 named independent ML and neuroscience alternatives, and establishes no access, derivation probability, or intent finding.

Graziano & Kastner (2011) establish Attention Schema Theory as a social/perceptual model of attention while lacking buildable artificial neural architectures, auxiliary internal-state self-prediction, and weight/RLCT complexity regularization. Between 2018 and 2024-2026 (reaching full 9-family join in Premakumar, Graziano et al. 2024 arXiv v1 and persisting in 2026 Nature Machine Intelligence VoR), the program assembles all 9 joined families. Conservative Lens 4 result is LSM-COMPONENT-SHIFT (quantitative-not-calibrated; access, copying, and intent unproven; 10 independent lineages including Graziano 2011 AST and Watanabe SLT credited).
